summary: Rev 2 resolves ARCH-1..3: file persistence in scope with atomic writes, request/note caps, strict X-User validation with loopback default. Residual minor points noted.

criteria.description: Users, scope, limits, identity, persistence, logging, error contract explicit.
AC1-AC11 are concrete with statuses, check order, and named test values.
A1-A4 stated with blocking effect; A1 backed by loopback default and Q2 owner.
Zero-dependency node:http plus file repository is proportionate.
Scale (500 notes x 100 users, 2KB bodies) is trivially feasible for whole-file rewrite; NFR3 measurable.
Trust boundary explicit, Map storage, 404 for non-owners, no content in logs, 0600 file.
Seven risks with likelihood, impact, mitigation, owner.

findings.title: Crash-leftover temp file blocks restart
findings.detail: AC8 refuses to start on a leftover temp file, but NFR4 crashes mid-write can produce exactly that, causing manual recovery. Safe but operationally harsh; no runbook (artifact:.eccode/artifacts/brief.md#Acceptance Criteria AC8).
findings.recommendation: Document the recovery procedure in the README, or define safe temp-file handling at design.

findings.title: Distinct user count unbounded
findings.detail: Notes are capped per user but the number of users is not; relies on the gateway authenticating users (A1).
findings.recommendation: State a total-store cap or explicitly rely on the gateway in the README.

resolvedFindings.resolution: Fixed: R6, AC8, NFR4 add file persistence with atomic rename; Q1 has owner and date.
Fixed: R8, AC7 add 16 KB cap (413), 500-note cap (409), rate limiting assigned to gateway.
Fixed: AC6 regex, duplicate-header handling, __proto__ test, Map storage, AC9 loopback bind with warning.
